import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Dataset with continuous variable to bin
data = {
    'age': [18, 22, 25, 30, 35, 42, 48, 55, 62, 68, 72, 28, 33, 45, 58],
    'income': [25000, 35000, 42000, 55000, 68000, 82000, 95000, 110000, 130000, 150000, 170000, 40000, 60000, 88000, 120000]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Create age bins with custom labels
df['age_group'] = pd.cut(
    df['age'],
    bins=[0, 25, 35, 50, 65, 100],
    labels=['Young', 'Adult', 'Middle', 'Senior', 'Elderly']
)

# Create income bins using quantile-based binning
df['income_group'] = pd.qcut(
    df['income'],
    q=4,
    labels=['Low', 'Medium', 'High', 'Very High']
)

# Print the dataframe with both binned columns
print("Binned DataFrame:")
print(df)
print("\nAge group distribution:")
print(df['age_group'].value_counts().sort_index())
print("\nIncome group distribution:")
print(df['income_group'].value_counts().sort_index())
